ConnectionStrings.//Sentinel: Authenticates as postgres and immediately drops into the sentinel_app role, which switches superuser off — so the session has exactly the privileges sentinel_app will have. Connecting as sentinel_app directly is refused until pg_hba.conf on 192.168.2.151 gains a line for it; see deploy/README.md. Change Username to sentinel_app and remove Options once it does.

Database.//MigrateOnStartup: False in this host, always. Sentinel.Engine is the single writer of the schema — several API replicas racing to apply the same migration is how a half-migrated database happens.

Secrets.//Key: Base64 of 32 bytes. Encrypts the credentials held against each connection, so losing it means re-entering every one of them; changing it means moving the old value into PreviousKeys first.

//Outbound: Where the platform may send a request. This host uses it to refuse an endpoint when a connection is saved; Sentinel.Engine uses the same section again, against the address a name actually resolved to, at the moment it opens the socket. Keep the two in step: an endpoint this host accepts and the engine then refuses is a connection that saves cleanly and never works.

Outbound.//AllowLoopback: True only where a tester runs the service being called on the same machine as the engine. In a real deployment loopback is the platform itself, and a connection pointing at it is either a mistake or someone using Sentinel to reach a port they could not reach directly.
